We operate as a deliberately tight-knit, high-performing team where a Product Owner, Engineering Manager, Tech Lead, two Product Designers, and a dedicated full-stack engineering team ship fast, iterate constantly, and take full ownership of the end-to-end user journey. Most interface failures in e-commerce aren’t layout issues — they are communication problems: what is said, in what order, and on which screen. As Senior Product Design Engineer, you will own the end-to-end design of all customer-facing surfaces across five markets. You will also manage our design system, Maia (our AI shopping assistant), and provide the design guidance that powers our automated coding workflows. Why this role is exciting High-impact Group scope: Design every customer-facing touchpoint across web, iOS, and Android for five international markets, impacting millions of orders. True end-to-end ownership: Lead the complete lifecycle of product design — from initial problem definition and customer research to shipped A/B tests and real-world performance analysis. AI-first execution: Rohlik is an AI-first company. You’ll own the interface design for Maia, our AI shopping assistant, and build the structured design system guidance used by AI coding agents to generate on-brand code without hand-coding interfaces. Direct customer engagement: Lead user research and usability testing sessions directly with real shoppers, rather than commissioning external agencies or receiving filtered insights. High accountability, low overhead: Work in a small, autonomous team where design decisions move straight to production and work that doesn't deliver measured impact is honestly reverted. What you will own and deliver Customer Surfaces: Own the end-to-end design and UX strategy across web, iOS, and Android for all core journey stages: homepage, search & browse, product pages, basket, slot selection, checkout, and order tracking. Design System as a Product: Own component architecture, design tokens, patterns, and documentation, ensuring our coding agents have precise design guidance to generate accurate interfaces. AI Experience Design: Define the interaction patterns for Maia (our AI shopping assistant), governing when it intervenes, how it presents information, and how it hands over to human support. jobs.title: Senior Specialist, Market Planning
jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><h2><span data-sheets-root="1">About Wolt</span></h2> <p><span data-sheets-root="1">At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we’re building the delivery of (almost) everything and you’ll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.<br><br>Working at Wolt isn’t always easy, but it’s definitely exciting. Here you’ll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You’ll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you’re a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.</span></p></div><p>At Wolt, keeping courier supply healthy across every city we operate in is core to a great experience for both customers and couriers. As we've scaled to dozens of countries and hundreds of cities, planning &amp; managing supply has grown from a market-by-market exercise into a global challenge: we need a system that plans well everywhere at once, from our largest metros to our smallest cities.</p> <p>That's where this role comes in. jobs.title: MAIT Additive Manufacturing Materials Intern
jobs.description: Here at The Exploration Company, we are building spacecrafts for humanity. We want you as a talented MAIT Additive Manufacturing Materials Intern to help us in our mission by contributing to Additive Manufacturing (AM) materials development, qualification, and in-house production for our vehicles Nyx Earth, Nyx Moon, and Storm. The ideal candidate will support the development and qualification of materials for additive manufacturing applications. This includes supporting material characterization campaigns, powder management, process parameter development, quality activities, and technical manufacturing documentation. Role Overview As a MAIT Additive Manufacturing Materials Intern , you will gain hands-on experience across the lifecycle of critical spaceflight hardware, from early development stages through qualification and production. You will support the development, characterization, qualification, and industrialization of materials for Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) technologies. You will contribute to material characterization campaigns, new alloy development, powder management, process parameter development, manufacturing documentation, and quality-related activities. Working as part of the LPBF Team and closely in collaboration with the AM Operations Team, as well as Propulsion and Quality teams, you will help us advance our additive manufacturing capabilities and support the delivery of flight-ready components across TEC's propulsion, launch vehicle, and space systems programs. Key Responsibilities Support material characterization campaigns with internal test laboratories, external testing partners and assist in the analysis and interpretation of powder, metallurgical, microstructural, and mechanical testing data. Support materials and process development activities, including alloy development, process parameter development, material characterization, and heat treatment optimization. Assist with LPBF build preparation, process monitoring, and post-build evaluation. Operate LPBF machines and associated equipment as required and following appropriate training. Prepare structured build reports and material test data summaries, ensuring consistent documentation. Support the creation and continuous improvement of work instructions, manufacturing procedures, qualification documentation, and standardized reporting templates. Support quality improvement activities, including non-conformance investigation support, data collection, and corrective action tracking. Required Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Metallurgy, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. Good fundamentals in materials science, material characterization methodologies, and mechanical testing. Strong interest in additive manufacturing technologies and aerospace applications. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills. Attention to detail and the ability to document technical work clearly and consistently. Ability to work effectively within multidisciplinary and international teams. Fluent in English. Preferred Qualifications Completed a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Metallurgy, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field. Experience with LPBF technology. Experience with metallography, microscopy, powder characterization, or mechanical testing. Knowledge of aerospace materials such as nickel-based superalloys, titanium alloys, copper alloys, and stainless steels. Experience working in a laboratory, manufacturing, or research environment. Experience preparing laboratory reports, build reports, work instructions, test documentation, or technical procedures. Skilled in Excel, Python, R, or similar tools for data analysis and visualization. Why you should join us! This is a unique opportunity to define how rockets are built at scale. The pilot plant is the blueprint for the production lines that follow, and the robotic cells you lead will handle containers, motor casings and energetic materials every day. About us We're a Germany-based rocketry startup currently in stealth mode, scaling up rapidly to meet the demand for high-performance, reliable, and scalable solid propulsion technologies for space and defense applications. jobs.title: (Senior) React Native Engineer (m/f/x) - Based in Germany
jobs.description: Cara Care, a digital health company backed by Bayer AG, is on a mission to improve people’s digestive health through technology. As we expand our product portfolio and modernize our platform, we’re looking for a versatile, pragmatic, and forward-thinking (Senior) React Native Engineer (m/f/x) to help shape the future of digital therapeutics. Your Role You’ll join a cross-functional product team with high ownership, lean processes, and a clear focus: deliver real impact to patients. We’re looking for someone who thrives on solving real-world problems with code, is technology-open, and knows when to build fast and when to build right. You’ll also help us use AI tools and coding agents thoughtfully in day-to-day engineering, turning emerging capabilities into reliable workflows that improve how we design, build, test, and operate patient-facing products. Your Responsibilities Design, build, and ship high-quality React Native apps for iOS and Android with TypeScript . Use AI coding agents to implement features, refactor code, and generate tests. Define clear tasks and constraints, provide relevant context, and validate the resulting changes through code review, automated tests, and checks on real devices. Own the full mobile lifecycle : architecture, implementation, automated testing, release management, monitoring, and iteration. Integrate native capabilities (push notifications, deep links, biometric auth, camera/sensors); write and maintain native modules when needed (Swift/Kotlin). Drive mobile performance and reliability (startup time, bundle size, memory, battery) and meet accessibility best practices. Set up and evolve mobile CI/CD (e.g., Fastlane, GitHub Actions/Bitrise), internal testing (TestFlight/Play Console), and release pipelines. Collaborate closely with Product, Design, and Medical to explore, define, and deliver patient-centric features, and to improve our current platform. Connect AI-assisted development workflows to design and engineering tools via MCP , for example to access Figma specifications and components, check implementations against designs, and automate repetitive coding and validation tasks. Keep patient data, credentials, and other sensitive information out of unapproved tools and workflows. Uphold technical excellence in architecture, code quality, and security, especially in a regulated healthcare environment , including applicable requirements under IEC 62304, BSI TR-03161, and the MDR. Contribute to a platform that powers multiple regulated digital health products across indications like IBS, GERD, and upcoming expansions . Mentor other developers and help raise the technical bar across the team. Requirements Your Profile 5+ years of professional software engineering experience, with at least 3 years focused on React Native and shipping production apps. Expert with React Native and TypeScript, React Navigation, state management, and testing (Jest, React Native Testing Library; Detox a plus). Hands-on experience using AI coding agents to implement features, refactor code, and write automated tests, including connecting agents to engineering tools via MCP. You can explain how you scoped the work, verified the results, and handled tool permissions and sensitive data. Proven track record delivering to App Store and Google Play, including handling certificates/provisioning, in-app updates, and staged rollouts. Solid understanding of mobile security and privacy: secure storage, keychain/keystore, certificate pinning, data minimization, and PII handling. Experience with mobile CI/CD and release automation (Fastlane, GitHub Actions or Bitrise), and tools like Sentry. Product mindset : you’ve worked in product-centric teams, collaborated closely with non-technical stakeholders, and care deeply about UX and accessibility. Bonus : experience in regulated industries, healthcare, or other security-conscious environments; native iOS/Android development (Swift/Kotlin) 💡 Please note : Cara Care is a remote-firs

jobs.title: Kundensupport (m/w/d)
jobs.description: Angefangen hat alles vor sieben Jahren als ambitionierte Idee. Heute sind wir Marktführer für Abschlusszeitungen in Deutschland. Jedes Jahr nutzen mehr als zwei Drittel aller deutschen Abschlussjahrgänge die nuggit App, um ihre Abschlusszeitung und ihre Abschlusstextilien zu gestalten und sich damit eine Erinnerung an eine gemeinsame Zeit zu schaffen, die bleibt. Unsere Mission: Durch digitale Innovation und persönlichen Kundenkontakt sind wir für SchülerInnen der verlässliche Partner bei ihrem allerersten großen Projekt. Dafür hinterfragen wir permanent den Status Quo und entwickeln neue, kreative Lösungen. Wir sind ein kleines Team mit sehr großer Reichweite. Unsere Kunden sind SchülerInnen, die gerade ihre Abizeitung oder ihre Abschlusstextilien planen. Für viele ist das ihr erstes großes Projekt. Im Kundensupport (m/w/d) bist du ihre erste Anlaufstelle: per Chat, Telefon und Videocall, von der ersten Frage bis zur Lieferung. Standardfragen beantworten bei uns Chatbot und Helpcenter, du bist überall da, wo ein Mensch gebraucht wird. Das heißt viel direkter Kontakt, schnelles Feedback und echte Verantwortung. Aufgaben Support: Du beantwortest Anfragen unserer SchülerInnen per Chat, Telefon und E-Mail. Schnell, freundlich und so, dass sie danach wirklich weiterkommen. Problemlösung: Wenn etwas hakt, etwa bei Freigaben, Bestellungen oder Lieferterminen, findest du gemeinsam mit unserem Operations-Team eine Lösung und hältst den Jahrgang auf dem Laufenden. Begleitung: Du begleitest Jahrgänge von der Angebotsannahme bis zur Lieferung und sorgst dafür, dass kein Projekt untergeht. Video-Sprechstunden: Du führst buchbare Video-Calls, in denen SchülerInnen intensive Unterstützung bei ihrem Projekt bekommen. Self-Service: Du erkennst, welche Fragen immer wiederkommen, und hilfst dabei, Chatbot und Helpcenter besser zu machen. Feedback: Du gibst weiter, was SchülerInnen bewegt, damit wir Produkt und Abläufe verbessern können. So arbeiten wir Wir sprechen die Sprache unserer Kunden. Unsere Kunden sind 17, 18 oder 19 Jahre alt. Sie melden sich nach der Schule, in der Pause oder kurz vor der Deadline. Sie brauchen jemanden, der geduldig erklärt, verlässlich zurückmeldet und ehrlich sagt, wenn es eng wird. Automatisierung entlastet dich, sie ersetzt dich nicht. Chatbot, Helpcenter und Onboarding-Videos nehmen dir die Standardfragen ab, damit du Zeit für die Gespräche hast, die wirklich zählen. Eigeninitiative ist Pflicht, nicht Bonus. Du bekommst Ziele und Kontext, den Weg gestaltest du selbst. Niemand treibt dich an, aber alle verlassen sich auf dich. Hybrid, ehrlich gemeint. Unser neues Office liegt im Mindspace in der Uhlandstraße 32, direkt am Kudamm und bestens angebunden, mit allen Annehmlichkeiten eines Coworking Space. Alle weiteren Mindspace Standorte kannst du temporär mitnutzen. Homeoffice und mobiles Arbeiten sind selbstverständlich möglich, solange das Ergebnis stimmt. Qualifikation Du hast Erfahrung im Kundenservice oder Support, idealerweise mit Endkunden. Quereinstieg ist ausdrücklich willkommen, etwa aus Hospitality, Hotellerie, Gastronomie, Einzelhandel oder Jugendarbeit. Du kannst gut mit jungen Menschen: locker im Ton, verbindlich in der Sache und geduldig, wenn dieselbe Frage zum dritten Mal kommt. Du schreibst schnell, klar und freundlich. Am Telefon bist du genauso entspannt wie im Chat. Du behältst auch bei vielen parallelen Anfragen den Überblick. Unsere Saison hat klare Peaks. Du lieferst zuverlässig und meldest dich, bevor jemand nachfragen muss. Du arbeitest sicher mit digitalen Tools wie Chat-, Ticket- oder CRM-Systemen. Du sprichst fließend Deutsch. Das ist bei uns Voraussetzung, weil unsere Kunden deutschsprachig sind. Du hast eine proaktive Haltung und arbeitest gerne eng mit anderen Teams zusammen. Benefits Unser Angebot Du begleitest jedes Jahr Abschlussjahrgänge aus ganz Deutschland bei ihrem allerersten großen Projekt Eine Rolle mit Perspektive: Wenn du willst, übernimmst du Schritt für Schritt mehr Ve

Als Marketing Lead entwickelst du die passenden Ideen und Maßnahmen, um neue Kunden zu gewinnen und unser Wachstum aktiv voranzutreiben. Du willst Marketing nicht nur umsetzen, sondern verantworten – mit klaren Pipeline-Zielen, eigenem Budget und einem Team, das du weiterentwickelst? Als Marketing Lead bei ZEP übernimmst du die Ergebnisverantwortung für unser Marketing und die daraus entstehende Pipeline. Du führst das Marketingteam sowie unsere Agenturen und Dienstleister, steuerst das Marketingbudget und greifst aktiv ein, wenn Zahlen vom Plan abweichen. Dabei arbeitest du eng mit Sales und der Geschäftsführung zusammen. Du verbindest strategisches Denken mit einer Hands-on-Mentalität dort, wo es darauf ankommt. Deine Aufgaben Du verantwortest unsere Pipeline-Ziele und das Marketingbudget und steuerst aktiv gegen, wenn Zahlen abweichen. Du entwickelst die Marketingstrategie gemeinsam mit der Geschäftsführung, schärfst Positionierung und Messaging für unsere B2B-Zielgruppen und leitest daraus Ziele und Prioritäten ab. Als Teil des Management-Teams bringst du die Marketingperspektive in strategische Entscheidungen auf Unternehmensebene ein und gestaltest die Weiterentwicklung von ZEP aktiv mit. Du führst das Marketingteam, setzt Prioritäten und entwickelst die Teammitglieder fachlich und persönlich weiter. Du steuerst und forderst unsere Agenturen und Dienstleister – insbesondere im Paid-Bereich (z. B. Google Ads, Paid Social) – mit klaren Zielen und Briefings und misst sie an ihren Ergebnissen. Du baust Demand Generation über mehrere Kanäle auf, nicht nur über Paid. Du verbesserst gemeinsam mit dem Vertrieb die Lead-Qualität und die Übergabe an Sales. Du sorgst für sauberes Tracking und Attribution über den gesamten Funnel. Du wertest Kampagnen, Funnel und Conversion Rates aus – wenn nötig selbst in HubSpot und im Tracking – und leitest daraus konkrete nächste Schritte ab. Du entwickelst SEO und die Sichtbarkeit in KI-Suchen (AI Search) als wachsenden Kanal weiter. Du entwickelst unsere Website weiter und holst mehr Leads aus dem vorhandenen Traffic. Deine Voraussetzungen Du bringst mehrere Jahre Erfahrung im B2B-SaaS-Marketing mit, mit Schwerpunkt Demand Generation. Du hast nachweislich Pipeline- oder Umsatzziele erreicht und hattest Budgetverantwortung. Du hast bereits Führungserfahrung gesammelt: Du hast ein Marketingteam geführt, Prioritäten gesetzt und Mitarbeitende weiterentwickelt. Du hast Erfahrung darin, Agenturen und Dienstleister zu steuern und fachlich zu fordern. Du kennst dich mit Performance Marketing (Google Ads, Paid Social) so gut aus, dass du Agenturen auf Augenhöhe führst. Du bist sicher in Analyse, Tracking und Attribution; idealerweise hast du Erfahrung mit HubSpot. Du setzt KI selbstverständlich in deiner Arbeit ein und weißt, wo sie echten Mehrwert bringt. Du bringst eine Hands-on-Mentalität mit und wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jeder nächste Schritt vorgegeben wird. Du verfügst über sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und kannst dich auch auf Englisch sicher verständigen. Deine Benefits 30 Tage Urlaub und unbefristete Arbeitsverträge Remote First Company – Arbeite innerhalb Deutschlands von wo du möchtest! Unterstützung bei der Home-Office Einrichtung Chancen, Freiheiten und Mitgestaltungsmöglichkeiten eines Startups verbunden mit der Sicherheit eines seit über 20 Jahren etablierten Unternehmens im Mittelstand. Flexible Arbeitszeiten – Keine Kernarbeitszeiten, stimme dich einfach mit dem Team ab. Windows oder Mac? Entscheide selbst! 50 EUR monat

jobs.description: (Fully remote, async-first, DevTools SaaS, 32-40h/week, time zones: UTC-3 to UTC+3) The best developers don't wait for a customer to tell them something's broken. They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly's whole reason to exist. We give developers and their agents the tools to own reliability the way they own their code: end-to-end tests and synthetic monitoring defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, versioned and reviewed like everything else they ship. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place. Thousands of them, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password, build with us. In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel. Here's the thing about 2026: AI agents and coding assistants are shipping more software, faster, than any team could review by hand, and more of it is breaking in ways nobody has seen before. LLM-backed features fail probabilistically. Agents take actions no runbook anticipated. "Is my app healthy?" is becoming an unanswerable question for a whole generation of AI-native software. You will build reliability for this kind of software. Our stack is AI (Codex, Claude, use what you like best), Vue.js, TypeScript, Node.js, Golang, Postgres, ClickHouse and AWS. We ship to prod all day, every day. We practice Agile (not scrum) and take pride in good documentation and good looking products. We’re a remote-first startup that keeps things simple—low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love building cool things, working async, actually listening to and working with customers, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in! What you'll do Build and ship with AI You will actively use coding agents for full stack development, from exploring solutions and generating scaffolding to refactoring, test generation and debugging. At Checkly we push the limits of AI tools every day. Talk to our users You will talk directly to the developers, DevOps and Site Reliability Engineering (SRE) teams who are on-call, debugging incidents, or wiring Checkly into production pipelines. You will understand their workflows, pain points, and feedback. You use those conversations to validate ideas, course-correct early, and iterate on what you build. Customer calls and the weekly support rotation are part of the job, not a distraction from it. Find the right problems to solve In a world where the cost of building software trends to zero, the hard part is picking what to build. You will focus on real developer pain: flaky tests and flaky checks, unclear failures, noisy alerts. You will favour pragmatic solutions that ship quickly, validate assumptions in production, and compound into long-term reliability improvements. Own your work end to end From shaping the initial idea, through implementation and rollout, to watching how it behaves in production. You will take part in on-call and help support customers when things don’t work as expected. What you should have You have shipped features with AI, not just experimented with them. You have taken work from zero to shipped with a comparable stack, made implementation decisions that held up, and put things in front of real users. You have built and run production software. You know the realities of operating software that people depend on: edge cases, incidents, regressions, and the need for observability and follow-up. You are not surprised when things break. You help fix them. You can hold a product conversation, not just a technical one. You can look at a customer problem and reason about whether the thing we are about to build actually solves it. You work well without an office around you. You are autonomous and self-motivated in a remote setup, and you still enjoy getting to know your colleagues and helping other people get unstuck. jobs.description: <div class="content-intro"><h4><strong>Who We Are</strong></h4> <p>WPP Enterprise Solutions designs, builds, and operates the growth systems that competitive businesses rely on. In a world where Al is reshaping how companies drive growth, we lead clients in business transformation and marketing modernization, connecting strategy directly to execution. Our 12,000 experts in engineering and platforms, commerce, consulting, content transformation, CRM, and CX work within a unified global operating unit across 40+ markets. WPP Enterprise Solutions works alongside best-in-class partners including Adobe, AWS, Braze, Google, Microsoft, Salesforce, and Shopify, as well as innovators in AI, to deliver growth solutions tailored to the needs of our clients’ businesses. VML, part of WPP, supports WPP Enterprise Solutions by helping brands activate transformation through creativity and experience.</p></div><p>We are looking for a Principal Solutions Architect to join us on a permanent basis.&nbsp;<br><br>Our Commerce &amp; Technology division helps leading global brands design, build and run the commerce platforms behind their growth. We are seeking a Principal Solutions Architect to lead solution in business pursuits and account growth, across enterprise commerce.&nbsp;</p> <p>You will be the person in the room who understands how the whole commerce estate fits together, from web storefront and mobile app through commerce platform, data and ERP.&nbsp;&nbsp; You will turn that understanding into a clear case for business value, win the trust of senior client stakeholders, and when it helps, build a working demonstration to show them what good looks like.<strong>&nbsp;<br>&nbsp;</strong></p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Architect Enterprise Commerce: Design end to end commerce solutions across Adobe Commerce, Salesforce Commerce Cloud, Shopify, HCL and composable (MACH) solutions, spanning web, mobile apps, data and back office systems.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> </ul> <ul> <li>Lead with value: Frame every solution around commercial outcomes, cost and return, so clients can see clear cases for change rather than a technology shopping list.&nbsp;&nbsp;</li> </ul> <ul> <li>Serve as an outward-facing, energetic leader who runs workshops, participates in governance, and collaborates with commercial teams to identify and shape technical growth opportunities.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <p><strong>What you’ll be doing&nbsp;</strong></p> <ul> <li>Client Engagement and Discovery: Build trusted relationships with senior business and technology stakeholders. Run discovery workshops, ask the questions that uncover what really matters, and cut through complexity to the decisions that count.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <ul> <li>Solution Design and Architecture: Produce clear architecture diagrams and solution designs covering storefront, mobile apps, commerce platform, search, content, order management, product information, payments, data and other integrations. Recommend the right platform and approach for each client rather than defaulting to one.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <ul> <li>Platform Selection and Replatforming: Guide clients through platform choices and migrations, including the move from monolithic to composable, weighing total cost of ownership, speed to market, risk and operating model.&nbsp;</li> </ul> <ul> <li>Data, Integration and Back Office: Get into the detail of how commerce connects to ERP (such as SAP, Microsoft Dynamics or Oracle), order management, warehouse, customer data and analytics, and design integration patterns that hold up at enterprise scale.&nbsp;&

jobs.title: Staff Product Manager
jobs.description: Location: Chancery Lane, London (Office-based 4 days) The Mission At Fyxer, we believe the only sustainable competitive advantage for a startup is the quality and speed of execution. We are looking for a Product Lead who operates like a Staff PM: someone who owns our most important product bets end-to-end, from ambiguous problem space to shipped outcome. You combine sharp product judgment with hands-on discovery skills, and you measure yourself on commercial impact, not output. We're not looking for someone to write specs and manage a backlog. We want someone who helps us think better, decide better, and ship better. The goal isn't more process, it's higher quality decisions made faster. You will work directly with our Head of Product, CTO, founders and senior engineers to shape what we build and why. What you will own You will not hand anything over. You will own the bet from first insight to shipped impact. Own discovery through delivery for our most important product bets, from early ambiguity to validated direction to launched product Work directly with engineers and founders from the start of any initiative as the accountable product owner, not a coordinator Frame the problem, define the hypothesis, and choose the fastest route to signal: interviews, prototypes, fake doors, experiments, or just shipping and measuring Translate messy qualitative and quantitative signals into clear product direction, then drive that direction through to execution Set success metrics, make the call on when there's enough signal to build, and own the outcome either way Embed structured learning loops into how we operate so insight compounds over time Raise the bar of product thinking across the team: coach others, introduce lightweight frameworks, and get the whole company closer to customers Who you are You are a full-stack product thinker. Outcome owner: You connect user behaviour to funnels, retention, and revenue. You think in bets and expected value, not feature lists, and you hold yourself accountable to results. Discovery-strong: Genuinely fluent across qualitative research, behavioural insight, and experimentation. You generate strong signal quickly and pick the right method for the decision at hand, rather than outsourcing the thinking. Engineering partner: You work shoulder to shoulder with engineers, translating insight into crisp problem framing and practical tradeoffs. Engineers want to work with you because you make the work clearer, not slower. Decision oriented: You know when there's enough signal to move. You sharpen hypotheses, clarify thinking, and make confident calls under uncertainty. You'd rather ship and learn than perfect and wait. Force multiplier: Your impact shows up in how the whole team operates. You build repeatable systems for discovery and decision-making that outlast any single project. The Role You will be the senior product voice on our most important initiatives, working directly with the Head of Product, CPGO, founders, and senior engineers. This is not a support function. You will be embedded in high impact work from day one, with real authority over what we build and why. You will operate at speed. We care about generating signal quickly, making informed decisions, and shipping fast. You are comfortable working with imperfect information and tightening your thinking as you go. You will move fluidly across the full product lifecycle. Some weeks you will be deep in user interviews or pressure testing a major bet, other weeks you will be in the detail with engineers getting something over the line. You will have significant autonomy. We expect strong judgment, clear communication, and ownership of outcomes. If there are specific tools you believe are critical to moving faster or generating better signal, we will support that. We want you to design the right setup, not work around constraints. Why Fyxer? jobs.title: Deployment Strategist
jobs.description: The Role Procurement and supply chain is a $3 trillion market still running on outdated systems and manual processes. Magentic is changing that. We’re building a new generation of agentic AI that works inside the world’s largest and most complex organisations, backed by Sequoia and built by a team from OpenAI, Meta, Revolut, NASA and McKinsey. We’re early, moving fast and already solving real problems for global enterprises. As a Deployment Strategist , you’ll be at the heart of making that happen. You’ll take what we build and turn it into real-world impact for our customers, owning engagements from initial scoping through to live deployment. You’ll sit at the intersection of product, commercial and customer, figuring out what needs to be built, how we make it work and how we deliver meaningful outcomes. You won’t just be deploying Magentic, you’ll help shape how we work with customers as we scale. What You’ll Do You’ll have a huge impact on both Magentic’s commercial success and our product direction. This is a rare opportunity to help build a rocket ship. As we grow, you could develop into product management or engineering, into a leader in our customer engineering space, even into sales, as you discover your strengths and interests. Own deployments end-to-end —design the rollout strategy at household-name enterprises, run the programme, and change course decisively when the approach isn't landing. Hold the senior relationships —be the Director and VP sponsor's first call, run steering governance, and take on the difficult conversations. Find the value nobody has scoped —go looking beyond the signed scope, prove new use cases with the customer, and build the case for what we sell them next. Define best practice for AI deployment —set the bar on your deployments, and turn this into processes that the rest of the org can use to scale. Shape our roadmap —bring product and engineering the problem, the customer evidence, and a view on what we should build. You Might Be a Great Fit if You Have 5+ years of experience in a customer-facing delivery or product role Have managed complex, multi-stakeholder projects at senior levels and kept them moving when priorities shifted Think commercially: you track outcomes, not just activities, and you understand how successful deployments translate into revenue Are energised by early-stage ambiguity — you can create structure where none exists and make decisions with incomplete information Communicate exceptionally well, both in the room with a VP and in a written handover to a colleague Bonus Points Have experience deploying AI, automation, or data products inside large organisations Are familiar with procurement, supply chain, or finance functions in enterprise settings Compensation and Benefits At Magentic, we recognise and reward the talent that drives our success. We offer: Competitive Equity : play a real part in Magentic’s upside A salary of £100-110k Enhanced parental leave 25 days holiday exc bank holidays, plus an extra day for our Christmas shutdown In-office lunches provided Salary sacrifice pension and nursery schemes Hybrid London HQ (4 days per week onsite, with flex if you have appointments etc) Annual team retreat —a fully-funded off-site to recharge, bond, and build Our Interview Process We can move quickly through these stages, so let us know if you have any timelines we need to meet. Initial call (30 mins) : this first step is an opportunity for you to hear more about Magentic and the role, and for us to learn more about how your experience aligns with the role. Skills interview (45 mins): in this step, we'll ask you to prepare a presentation and take Q&A. In-person interview (half-day, paid): for the final step, we invite you to come meet the team in-person. We find this is the best way for candidates to get a sense of what working at Magentic is like. This day will include a culture interview, founder interview and a presentation task / discussion with the team. Equal

jobs.description: <p data-pm-slice="1 1 []">SLSQ427R384</p> <p>At Databricks, we help public institutions use data and AI to improve services, increase productivity, and get more value from public data and technology investment. That means putting trusted, relevant insight closer to the people making operational, policy and service decisions, and building services that can evolve as missions, technology and delivery models change, rather than becoming tomorrow's legacy.</p> <p>Databricks is looking for an Account Executive to own and grow some of our most strategic Public Sector customers in the UK government delivering against their core missions. You will inherit an established portfolio of strategic government accounts, with a clear mandate to protect and expand that base while building new relationships across departments and agencies we do not yet serve.</p> <p>This is a succession role: you will step into relationships and momentum that already exist, building trust quickly with current stakeholders while developing your own view of where Data and AI can help solve the sector's most important challenges. You will translate national and departmental priorities into measurable customer outcomes and sustainable growth.</p> <p>Working closely with government stakeholders, internal teams, cloud providers, and strategic partners, you will deepen consumption in existing accounts and extend Databricks' footprint.</p> <h2><strong>The Pressures Shaping This Work</strong></h2> <p>Government's hardest missions increasingly require insight across institutional boundaries, without requiring those institutions, their accountability, or their data to be centralised. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.</span></p> <p><span style="font-weight: 300; font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif;">Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. jobs.title: Trust Communications
jobs.description: TL;DR Millions of people build on Lovable, from software that runs new businesses to the tools that power existing ones. At the center of it all is trust. That’s why we’re looking for an exceptional storyteller to spearhead Lovable’s trust, safety, and security communications efforts. Why Lovable For decades, the ability to build software belonged to a tiny fraction of the population: the people with the credentials, the technical training, the access. Everyone else had to wait, or pay, or give up. Lovable is the counterargument: We exist for the people with ideas who were locked out of software creation until now. Over 70 million projects have been built on the platform. Hundreds of thousands of people pay for it. The product handles real infrastructure, not only prototypes: authentication, databases, payments, and deployment. People run real businesses on Lovable, which means the stakes are real too. The comms challenge: when anyone can build, the platform has to be safe for everyone who does, and they need to know it. That takes someone who can tell the story of how we think about topics like safety, security, and reliability before anyone asks, and who can be honest, precise, and fast when the questions come up anyway. What you’ll do Build and own Lovable’s trust narrative. You’ll own Lovable’s trust narrative in earned, new, and owned media, proactively telling the story of how we think about security, privacy, and safety. You’ll shape the stories that highlight our commitments and ensure we show up in the conversations where trust in AI platforms is being decided right now. Be the comms partner to our security and trust leadership. You’ll develop and own the spokesperson platforms for our CISO and other senior leaders who speak on our trust efforts, identifying and preparing them for on-stage and media opportunities. You’ll help them become recognized voices on topics of trust in AI software creation. Own incident communications, end to end. When something doesn’t go as planned, you’re the incident comms lead who ensures clear and swift communications for every audience that needs to hear from us, including media, customers, and employees. You’ll build and run the playbook that lets us move faster each time. Build relationships with relevant media and creators. You’ll know the voices who matter most in telling our trust story, and you’ll make sure those relationships exist before we need them. Who you are You’ve done trust, safety, or security communications. You have proven comms experience across a variety of trust-related topics, from AI safety to security. You’ve worked on or alongside security, privacy, or trust and safety teams. You have real incident experience. You’ve been the incident comms lead more than once, and you’ve probably written a playbook along the way. You bring the attention to detail, precision, speed, and judgment an incident requires. You have strong media relationships in the tech and AI ecosystem. Security and trust reporters, analysts, policy-adjacent media, perhaps even researchers. You know who they are, what they care about, and how to earn their attention honestly. You’re voraciously curious. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you need to be willing to understand how a platform like ours works well enough to describe an incident accurately and explain a safety decision without hand-waving. You write clearly and have keen attention to detail. Your writing is precise, human, and accessible, even when the subject matter is complex or the situation is sensitive. You also catch things others may miss. You’re calm, hands-on, and low-ego. You’ll draft the statements, build the media list, prep the spokesperson, and coordinate across teams yourself. You thrive in environments where the plan often changes and the pace is relentless. You have 6+ years of experience in communications , with significant time spent on trust and safety, security, or incident communications at a technology company. We

jobs.description: What do we do? Paddle offers digital product companies a completely different approach to their payment infrastructure. Instead of assembling and maintaining a complex stack of payments-related apps and services, we’re a Merchant of Record for our customers. We're hiring a Director of Self-Serve to take full commercial ownership of Paddle's self-serve motion, running and scaling it as a business line. Getting this right is a genuinely cross-functional endeavour, and your ability to bring people with you will be just as important as your commercial acumen. You'll operate with a small, focused team including engineering capacity. This is a role for someone who wants to build and run the engine hands on, not manage through layers. What you'll do Own the line. Carry the commercial number for self-serve end to end, from acquisition through adoption, to revenue and net retention. Own the unit economics, and how they improve. Define the customer profile that makes the economics work and work collaboratively with Demand Generation on the targeting you need, co-owning a single funnel against a shared ICP. Orchestrate cross-functionally. Codify the work into clear streams with clear owners, influence the Product, Engineering, and Risk roadmaps, and run a regular business cadence that keeps people aligned on priorities and impact. Deepen partner integrations. Work hand-in-glove with Partnerships to turn distribution relationships into deep well-integrated channels, owning the commercial outcome of partner-sourced volume. Build and run the engine. Design and run the experimentation, tooling, and tracking to improve funnel codification, time-to-value, activation, and conversion using AI where it raises velocity and quality, applied to the right customer. jobs.description: About BJAK BJAK is Southeast Asia’s largest digital insurance platform, expanding financial access through automation, data, and digital scale. As we grow across markets, we are committed to building a platform that is safe, compliant, and trusted. We are hiring a Senior Compliance Director – UK to lead regulatory strategy, risk governance, and compliance operations for our UK market entry and expansion alongside the CEO. This role is expected to hold the SMF16 (Compliance Oversight) Senior Management Function once approved, and will act as our primary point of contact with the FCA. This is a build role: you'll be creating frameworks, policies, and controls from scratch rather than inheriting an existing function. Why This Role Matters The Senior Compliance Director – UK will: Design and enforce compliance frameworks that enable safe scaling of digital financial services. Ensure BJAK operates in accordance with UK regulatory standards, especially FCA requirements. Protect consumers through transparent, fair, and ethical practices. Establish BJAK as a trusted partner with regulators, partners, and industry stakeholders. Build compliance capability and culture across the company. What You Will Do Regulatory Leadership & Strategy Develop and maintain compliance frameworks aligned with UK regulatory requirements. Lead regulatory readiness for market entry, licensing, and ongoing supervision. Serve as the primary contact with the FCA and relevant UK bodies. Interpret regulatory changes and guide business strategy accordingly. Risk Governance & Compliance Operations Build policies and controls covering AML, KYC, data privacy, consumer duty, distribution, and claims-related compliance. Conduct risk assessments and implement remediation plans for identified gaps. Establish monitoring, testing, and reporting processes for ongoing compliance. Ensure internal audits, compliance reviews, and control testing are operationalised. Consumer Protection & Business Integrity Embed fairness, transparency, and responsible selling throughout the organisation. Oversee product compliance, marketing reviews, pricing governance, and distribution oversight. Implement complaint handling frameworks aligned with regulatory standards. Cross-Functional Support & Training Partner with product, operations, legal, marketing, and commercial teams to ensure compliant execution. Provide guidance on regulatory implications of new products, partnerships, or distribution models. Deliver training to ensure teams understand and execute compliance responsibilities. You Will Thrive in This Role If You See compliance as a strategic enabler, not a blocker. Operate with high integrity, sound judgment, and strong attention to detail. Communicate clearly and influence leaders using data and logic. Enjoy building frameworks and scaling systems from early-stage to mature environments. Thrive in fast-paced, evolving settings where regulation meets innovation. What You Bring 8+ years of compliance, risk, or regulatory experience within financial services, insurance, insurtech, or fintech. Deep understanding of UK regulatory frameworks, including FCA rules and consumer duty requirements. Experience in compliance for digital platforms, distribution, or insurance products (preferred). jobs.title: Frontend Engineer
jobs.description: About ActAI There are over 5 billion users using basic applications today such email, notes, tasks, calendar and they're not AI-native. Our mission is to build proactive applications for anyone in the world, who are not used to complex prompting. We aim to bring intelligence to conversations, errands, organising and workflows, with minimal to no prompting. Our first application is an agent-first mobile communication app. We believe building applications that users use daily for communication, coordination and collaboration needs will help integrate AI into their lives. The net effect is to eliminate misinformation, achieve low coordination costs, enable high quality tasks and collaboration at scale with minimal or little prompting. Role As a Web Frontend Engineer, you will build the core web experiences, including Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs and Sheets. You will own complex, highly interactive product surfaces from architecture through implementation, working closely with product, design, backend and AI engineers to make AI a native part of how users communicate, write, organise and work. What You'll Own Build major web experiences across Chat, Notes, Calendar, Docs, and Sheets. Develop complex interactions including real-time messaging, collaborative editing, rich-text editing, scheduling, tables, and spreadsheets. Build reusable frontend architecture and components that work consistently across ActAI applications. Integrate streaming AI responses, proactive actions, and model-driven experiences directly into product workflows. Own frontend performance, responsiveness, reliability and accessibility across browsers and devices. Work closely with product and design to take ideas from prototype to production quickly. What We're Looking For Strong experience building complex, production web applications using React, TypeScript and modern frontend technologies. jobs.description: About Us Hawk is the leading provider of AI-supported anti-money laundering and fraud detection technology. Banks and payment providers globally are using Hawk’s powerful combination of traditional rules and explainable AI to improve the effectiveness of their AML compliance and fraud prevention by identifying more crime while maximizing efficiency by reducing false positives. With our solution, we are playing a vital role in the global fight against Money Laundering, Fraud, or the financing of terrorism. We offer a culture of mutual trust, support and passion – while providing individuals with opportunities to grow professionally and make a difference in the world. Your Mission As a Customer Data Scientist at Hawk, you're the person our customers trust to make their AML and fraud detection models actually work for them: tuned to their transaction patterns, defensible to their regulators, and provably effective in their own numbers. You sit inside the regional customer team, working directly alongside Customer Value Partners on live accounts, not behind a wall of tickets from a central data science function. Your work spans model and threshold tuning, deep analytical investigation into detection performance, and building the customer-facing narrative that shows exactly what's improved and why. You've done this in front of customers before, and you know the difference between a model that scores well in a notebook and one that survives contact with a real investigator's workload. Key Responsibilities Tune and optimize detection models and thresholds against each customer's live transaction data, balancing detection effectiveness against false positive load, not just against a benchmark dataset. Investigate detection performance deeply: dig into missed cases, alert quality, and pattern drift, and turn what you find into concrete tuning or configuration changes. Translate technical findings into customer-facing insight: build the analysis that shows investigator productivity gains, false positive cost reduction, and detection effectiveness improvements in language a customer's compliance and risk leadership actually uses. Sit in the room with customers directly. Present findings, defend your methodology to a customer's own data science or compliance team, and answer the hard “why did the model do this” questions live. Partner closely with your regional Customer Value Partners on account strategy, informing where the model needs to change to unlock the next stage of value realization or a renewal conversation. Feed patterns and findings back into Hawk's broader model and product functions, distinguishing between “this customer needs local tuning” and “this is a systemic gap worth fixing centrally.” Own the regulatory defensibility of the tuning decisions you make. Document your reasoning so a customer's audit or regulator review holds up. Bring rigor to how you validate model changes before they go live: backtesting, sample review, and sign-off discipline that protects the customer's compliance posture. Your Profile 5-7 years as a data scientist in a customer-facing role, presenting analysis and defending model decisions directly to clients. This is not an internal-facing engineering or product data science background; you've sat across the table from a customer before. Real experience in AML, fraud detection, or financial crime analytics is required. You understand transaction monitoring, typologies, and what a false positive actually costs an investigator, not just what one costs on a confusion matrix. Strong hands-on skills in the standard data science stack (Python, SQL, and whatever ML tooling you've used in production), but your edge is judgment under ambiguity: knowing when a model change is safe to make and when it needs a human in the loop. Founded in Cologne in 2018, we have built a profitable business across our own products and more than 700 partner pharmacies. Now we are bringing that to the UK. Medical cannabis is one of the fastest-growing areas of UK healthcare: around 140,000 people will be prescribed it in 2026, up from around 100,000 a year earlier. Yet an estimated 1.8 million people in the UK already use cannabis to manage a health condition, mostly outside the legal system. That is more than 10x today’s market, in a category that is still largely uncharted. We are building a clinic and platform that makes care simpler, faster and more personal. Our UK team is at an early stage, which means real ownership, real impact and the chance to shape how we work from day one. The role Location: London, 4 days a week in the office Reporting to: MD and Co-Founder UK Employment type: Full-time, permanent As Head of Growth, you will lead growth for enua UK: building our patient acquisition engine and shaping how the UK talks about medical cannabis as a legitimate treatment. This is a highly commercial, founding leadership role in the UK. You will own our growth strategy and budget, with the mandate to build the team and infrastructure to deliver it. You will sit on a small management team with our MD and Co-Founder, jointly responsible for the success of the business, and have a real say in product, pricing and go-to-market decisions. Tasks Leadership : Be a core member of our management team, jointly responsible for setting and delivering the strategy for the business. Build a high-performing, AI-first marketing team and get the best from our agencies and freelancers. Growth strategy and execution : Own the growth plan and budget. With the MD, set and deliver our patient acquisition strategy, including which channels we use and how much we invest in each. Partner with product and tech to improve conversion across our website and sign-up flow, and evolve our brand positioning as we learn from patients. Long-term value : Drive total net long-term value from every patient we acquire, optimising CAC, average revenue per patient and retention together. Focus on acquiring the right patients, not just more of them. Set targets and budgets with finance based on unit economics. Performance marketing : Own performance across all channels, including search and SEO, paid social, affiliates, partnerships, referral, offline and print. Tracking and reporting : Set up attribution, tracking and reporting from scratch, so every pound of spend is accountable, and report weekly on performance. Category awareness and PR : Build awareness and trust in medical cannabis and help reduce stigma. Set our PR strategy with our agency partners. CRM and retention : Shape the patient CRM journey to drive engagement and retention, working closely with our clinical team. Requirements A strategic, AI-first leader : 7+ years in marketing, with at least 3 in a senior or Head of role. You have led a team of 3 or more, been part of a leadership team and embedded AI in how a team works. Experienced performance marketer : Strong hands-on experience across search, SEO, paid social and funnel optimisation, with a track record of scaling spend at a healthy CAC and LTV:CAC. Partnerships experience is a real bonus. A builder : You have been an early hire in a founding team and helped take a consumer business from launch through rapid scale, building the growth engine rather than inheriting it. Sector-savvy : Background in D2C subscription, consumer health or another regulated category (healthcare, pharma, telehealth or similar), with a good grasp of repeat-purchase economics, CRM and advertising within

jobs.description: Présentation département L’Institut des Nanotechnologies de Lyon (INL) a pour vocation de développer des recherches technologiques multidisciplinaires dans le domaine des micro et nanotechnologies et de leurs applications. Les recherches menées s’étendent des matériaux aux systèmes. Le laboratoire s’appuie sur la plate-forme technologique lyonnaise Nanolyon. Les domaines d’application couvrent de grands secteurs économiques : l’industrie des semiconducteurs, les technologies de l’information, les technologies du vivant et de la santé, l’énergie et l’environnement. Le laboratoire est multi sites avec des localisations sur les campus d’Ecully et de Lyon-Tech La Doua. Il regroupe environ 240 personnes dont 120 personnels permanents. L’INL est un acteur majeur du Pôle de Recherche et d’Enseignement. Ce poste se situe dans un environnement innovant, à la pointe des technologies du futur, dans des secteurs stratégiques applicatifs. Le poste se situe dans un secteur relevant de la protection du potentiel scientifique et technique (PPST), et nécessite donc, conformément à la réglementation, que votre arrivée soit autorisée par l'autorité compétente du MESR Présentation de la ou les thématiques : Le programme PHOENIX est un projet national d’envergure (17 M€, 5 ans) financé par France 2030 et visant à structurer un hub français pour la conception de circuits intégrés, incluant les chiplets et les méthodes d’EDA enrichies par l’IA. Il implique plusieurs laboratoires du CNRS (INL, TIMA, IRISA, IETR, LIP6, LIRMM, LAMIH, IMS, Lab Hubert Curien, Lab-STICC…), le CEA-LIST, ainsi que de nombreux partenaires académiques et industriels. Dans ce cadre, nous recrutons un(e) ingénieur(e) informatique / EDA chargé(e) de la qualification des outils, modèles et blocs IP utilisés et développés au sein de PHOENIX, en interaction étroite avec les équipes de recherche, les doctorants et les partenaires industriels. Description de la ou les missions / les activités - Mettre en place, maintenir et faire évoluer l’environnement logiciel de conception (flow EDA) pour les partenaires du consortium PHOENIX (CAO, simulation, caractérisation, PDK, IP). - Qualifier les outils EDA (commercials et open source), modèles de dispositifs et blocs IP : définition de bancs de tests, métriques de performance, protocoles d’évaluation et rapports de validation. - Participer à l’intégration et à l’évaluation de méthodes d’EDA augmentées par l’IA (optimisation de flows, génération de modèles, analyse automatique de résultats, etc.). - Assurer le support technique auprès des équipes (installation, configuration, troubleshooting, interface avec les fournisseurs d’outils et les équipes IT locales). - Contribuer à la rédaction de livrables techniques du projet : documents de spécification, rapports de qualification, guides d’utilisation des outils et IP. - Mettre en place de bonnes pratiques pour la gestion de versions, la traçabilité des résultats, l’automatisation des flows (scripts, CI/CD, conteneurisation). - Participer à la veille technologique sur les outils EDA, les librairies IP, les technologies de calcul avancées et proposer des évolutions du parc logiciel. Profil recherché / Compétences attendues________________________________ Diplômes : Diplôme d’ingénieur, Master 2 ou doctorat en informatique, microélectronique ou domaine proche. Expérience : Débutant accepté Compétences opérationnelles : - Solides compétences en EDA (front-end et/ou back-end) : RTL, synthèse, P&R, extraction, simulation (SPICE, mixed-signal, etc.), PDK, caractérisation. - Maîtrise de scripts et automatisation (Python, Shell, Make, ou équivalent) et aisance avec les environnements Linux. - Connaissance souhaitée des architectures matérielles pour l’IA, des technologies émergentes ou de la conception de chiplets. - Intérêt marqué pour la qualité logicielle et la validation : tests, métriques, reproductibilité, documentation. - Excellent sens de la communication et du travail en équi

jobs.title: CENTRALE LYON - Post-Doctoral Position Ferroelectric-Based Ternary Computing: From Circuit Design to System-Level Integration Scientific Context
tags: inl - institut des nanotechnologies de lyon
jobs.description: Energy efficiency remains one of the foremost challenges in modern computing, spanning from edge IoT devices to high-performance data centers. Conventional CMOS-based architectures are approaching fundamental physical limits, while the "memory wall" — data transfers between processor and memory accounting for 70 to 90% of total system energy — continues to worsen with the ever-growing demands of data-intensive workloads such as deep neural networks and signal processing pipelines. In-Memory Computing (IMC) has emerged as a disruptive paradigm to overcome these bottlenecks by embedding arithmetic operations directly within memory arrays, drastically reducing data movement. In this landscape, ferroelectric field-effect transistors (FeFETs) stand out as particularly compelling devices: fully compatible with standard CMOS fabrication processes, non-volatile, reconfigurable, and capable of storing intermediate polarization states — a property that naturally enables ternary logic within a single device. The Post-Doctoral position will cover at least one of the following tasks: Design Standard Cell Technology Library based on FeFET devices developed at INL in order to be used with synthesis flow. Design and optimize ternary arithmetic units (multiply-accumulate units, adders, comparators) based on the FeFET ternary gate library developed within the project, targeting area, power, and timing closure under realistic process constraints. Develop and refine system-level models of FeFET-based ternary IMC units, abstracting circuit-level characterization results into architecture simulators, enabling design space exploration across the full heterogeneous system. Investigate hardware/software co-design strategies for mapping real-world applications — particularly convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and signal processing kernels — onto the ternary IMC fabric, exploiting approximate computing techniques to trade precision for energy efficiency. Assess and benchmark the energy, performance, and accuracy trade-offs of ternary IMC against binary CMOS and binary NVM-based IMC reference implementations, using both synthetic benchmarks and real application workloads. Contribute to the definition of a design methodology for ternary ferroelectric circuits, including EDA tool flows, cell library characterization guidelines, and design rules, with the aim of enabling broader community adoption. Required Candidate Profile The ideal candidate holds a PhD in microelectronics, computer architecture, or a closely related field , and demonstrates at least one of the following hard skills: Circuit and architecture design: Strong expertise in digital circuit design flows and computer architecture, with hands-on experience using industrial EDA tools (Cadence Virtuoso/Spectre, Synopsys). Experience with standard-cell library characterization is a plus. Emerging memory technologies: Solid knowledge of non-volatile memory devices, preferably including ferroelectric materials (FeFET, FeCap) or resistive memories (RRAM, PCM). Familiarity with compact modeling is an asset. System-level design and simulation: Experience with architecture-level simulation frameworks and hardware/software co-design methodologies. Knowledge of RISC-V ecosystems is a plus. Application domains: Familiarity with deep neural network inference workloads and/or digital signal processing pipelines, particularly in the context of approximate or energy-constrained computing. Programming: Proficiency in HDL (Verilog, VHDL, Verilog-A) and scripting languages (Python, Shell) for design automation and simulation. Soft skills: Scientific leadership, ability to coordinate with PhD students and international partners, strong publication record consistent with career stage, and excellent written and oral communication in English. Language: Fluent scientific English is mandatory. French is not required but is welcome. Find more English Speaking Jobs in France on Arbeitnow

Here at The Exploration Company, we are developing, producing, and operating Nyx, a modular and reusable space orbital vehicle that can eventually be refuelled in orbit, and which carries cargo – and potentially humans in the long run. We are also developing different types of propulsion systems to power our future vehicles and missions. As a talented Test Development Engineer , you will be part of the team that is responsible for the development of test facilities for our future propulsion systems. Key Responsibilities / Tasks: In your capacity as a Test Development Engineer , your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties may include: Synthesise test bench requirements from user and operator needs and plan required verification methods and tests. Translate engine test objectives and stakeholder needs into facility-level functional and performance requirements. Perform technical trade-offs to determine the best choice of hardware, software, equipment, component, location etc for various test facilities. Perform risk assessment analyses for future tests and developing mitigation actions to ensure personnel and hardware safety. Provide technical inputs to cost, schedule, procurement, commissioning, maintainability, and facility acceptance planning. Prepare and maintain P&IDs of test facilities based on test bench requirements and selecting components. Undertaking preliminary design of the ground support equipment with minimal oversight. Undertake hazard assessments of the test facility design (FMEA and HAZOPs) to determine if any additional changes to the design are required. Work with the current test bench team to coordinate end-to-end activities of the development of test facilities including design, reviews, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, test operations, ongoing upgrades and maintenance. Work with procurement, AIT and design teams during the development of test facilities to find the right balance of technical solutions, cost and lead time. Presenting findings to team members and participating in design reviews and project discussions. What we would love to see from you: Bachelor's, master's or PhD in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, or a related field (Master’s and above preferred). 2–5 years of experience in propulsion, test facility development, experimental engineering, or a related field. Practical experience in the design, development, commissioning, or operation of test facilities, preferably for rocket propulsion systems. Experience in test facility design for cryogenic propulsion systems is highly desirable. Relevant experience with other cryogenic or high-pressure fluid systems will also be considered. Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret technical data, challenge assumptions, and make evidence-based engineering recommendations. Proven ability to work autonomously on assigned technical topics while contributing effectively to a multidisciplinary engineering team. Excellent communication and leadership skills, with the ability to convey complex concepts to diverse audiences. Why you should join us! What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is: We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them We have a lot of Fun - we refuel our energy knowing we are democratising space. jobs.title: Lead Tech SRE
jobs.description: About Kestra Kestra is the universal orchestration platform : open source, declarative, and designed to orchestrate data pipelines, IT automation, business workflows, and AI/agentic systems. Trusted by over 10,000 organizations worldwide , including JPMorgan Chase, Bloomberg, FILA, and Crédit Agricole , Kestra orchestrates mission-critical workloads at scale. The open-source project has close to 30,000 GitHub stars , hundreds of contributors, and a fast-growing global community. About the role Kestra Cloud is our fully managed SaaS edition of Kestra. Each customer gets a dedicated Kestra instance on dedicated infrastructure, so the platform is a fleet of isolated stacks rather than one shared cluster. It is in Beta today, running production workloads for early customers, with General Availability planned for 2027. Each instance runs arbitrary user code (scripts, containers, queries against their own systems) through hundreds of plugins, and the fleet grows with every new customer. Provisioning, upgrading, and observing dozens to hundreds of identical stacks without drift is the core problem. We're looking for a Lead Tech SRE to own Kestra Cloud end to end: the architecture and specs, the delivery, the monitoring, and the continuous improvement of the platform. You decide how the platform should evolve, write it down, split it into work, and ship it with your team. You would lead a team of three, yourself included. That means you stay hands-on (a large share of your week is Terraform, Kubernetes manifests, and incident work) while setting the technical direction, reviewing designs, and dispatching work to two SREs. You work closely with the CTO, the platform engineering teams building the Kestra core, and our security engineer. This is an engineering leadership role, not a people-management-only one. What you would do Architecture & specs Own the target architecture of Kestra Cloud on GCP: the per-customer dedicated stack (cluster, network, databases, queues), how it is templated and versioned, regions, and the path from Beta to GA. Write the specs (design docs, RFCs, ADRs) that turn product needs into infrastructure work, and defend the trade-offs: cost per customer vs isolation level, GCP project vs cluster vs node pool per customer, managed service vs self-run. Define SLOs and error budgets per service and per tier, and make them the basis for prioritization. Delivery Break specs into work and dispatch it across the team, then review and unblock. You set the bar for Terraform modules, Helm charts, and GitOps conventions. Automate the customer instance lifecycle : provisioning, upgrades, scaling, backups, migration, and decommissioning, with no manual steps. Own the release path of Kestra Cloud with ArgoCD and GitHub Actions: progressive rollouts, rollback, and upgrade safety across the whole fleet of customer instances. Monitoring & operations Build the observability stack (metrics, logs, traces, alerting) so that issues are caught before customers report them. Run on-call and incident response for the team: rotation, runbooks, blameless postmortems, and follow-ups that actually ship. Plan capacity for a workload that is bursty by nature, and keep autoscaling honest. Continuous improvement Drive cost efficiency (FinOps) on GCP: per-customer cost visibility, right-sizing, committed use, and spot where it fits. Harden the platform with our security engineer: network policies, workload identity, secrets, and audit trails toward SOC 2 expectations. Feed back into the product : when Kestra itself makes the cloud hard to run, you write the issue, propose the fix, and work with core engineering to land it. Our Tech Stack Cloud : GCP (GKE, Cloud SQL, GCS, Cloud Load Balancing, IAM / Workload Identity) Infrastructure as Code : Terraform, Helm Orchestration : Kubernetes, Docker Deployment & Repository : GitHub Actions, ArgoCD Monitoring & Logs : OpenTelemetry, Elastic, Prometheus, Grafana Datastore : PostgreSQL, Elasti

Our vision We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones). We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business. In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to : 💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants 💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more... 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor . 🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe 🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings 🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France! The role of Financial Services in our strategy is set to grow, both in terms of revenue and product contribution, to serve our 800k current customer base. As such, we are initiating a process to get licensed as Etablissement de paiement et Société de financement. Our ambition is to start onboarding new customers by mid 2027 before starting migrating existing customers. To meet this ambition, we are starting to hire our Tech, Product, Compliance, Legal and Ops leaders. This position requires a strong understanding of quantum computing protocols on real hardware, strong software engineering skills and proficiency with AI tools. jobs.title: Photonic Integrated Circuit Designer Intern (H1/2027)
jobs.description: About Quandela Quandela stands as a global leader in quantum computing, driven by groundbreaking technology and a strategic vision for scaling quantum solutions. The company’s unique ability to offer both hardware and software solutions, along with its commitment to build energy efficient datacenters and scalability, positions it to play a key role in the next wave of innovation, and in many strategic and sovereign industrial sectors. Join Us at the Forefront of Quantum Computing Innovation 🚀 Description of the Team The internship will be conducted in the Photonic Integrated Circuits (PICs) department ofQuandela. The PICs team works on the production and development of the optical processors of Quandela quantum computers, having in mind performance and scalability. In detail, the team members carry out electromagnetic and thermal simulations to estimate the performance of the integrated components, prepare PICs layouts to be fabricated in collaboration with external foundries, and take care of both the characterization and the packaging of the fabricated devices. Your Key Responsibilities Depending on your experience and the duration of the internship, your work may involve deepening the understanding of existing building blocks, exploring new functionalities or tools, or developing advanced modeling approaches for testing. In particular, the goal of this internship will be to either bridge the gap between fabrication and design, or to evaluate new architecture for quantum processing unit (QPU). In this role you will be using standard electromagnetic simulations and/or circuit modelling by means of commercial software like Lumerical FDTD, FDE, EME or free-tools (gdsfactory, tidy3d, meow, sax..). This position is only valid with an Internship Agreement. Minimal duration is 5 months. Shorter internship will not be accepted. Ideal starting date late Summer 2026. General knowledge of integrated photonics modelling and layout Python, Git, Lumerical, simulation tools (FDTD, mode solver, EME..)
